title: TrajectoryRecord
description: One line of a run's `{stem}.trajectory.jsonl`, written by `autoware_carla_scenario.trajectory_recorder.TrajectoryRecorder`, format version 2: one of seventeen records, told apart by `type`. Units, frames and the order of a file: docs/trajectory_log.md.

WorldRecord.title: WorldRecord
WorldRecord.description: The first line of the file: the world the run recorded.

schema_version.description: The version of this format the file was written in: 2 (the records `map`, `warmup`, `actor_gone`, `markers`, `condition` and `result` were added in it). Absent from files of version 1, which have only `world`, `traffic_light`, `actor` and `tick` records.

episode.description: The CARLA episode id (`world.id`): a random uint64 in LibCarla, so up to 2^64 - 1 -- past what a double holds exactly: read it as a 64-bit unsigned integer (JavaScript: a BigInt-aware parser). It only tells episodes apart.

MapRecord.title: MapRecord
MapRecord.description: The map files the run read, written once, right after `world` (version 2). Each file is named and hashed, so a reader can find the very map the run was on and tell it from another; a field is null when the run had none.

name.description: The CARLA map the runs load, its short name (e.g. "Town10HD_Opt").

source.description: Where the map came from, as the run's `map.source` named it (e.g. "git+https://huggingface.co/datasets/OWNER/NAME@REV#PATH"), or `map.directory`; null when the config named neither.

lanelet2.description: The Lanelet2 map (.osm) the run read, or null when it read none.

opendrive.description: The OpenDRIVE (.xodr) the run read its road network from, or null.

projector_info.description: The Lanelet2 map's `map_projector_info.yaml`, as read (e.g. {"projector_type": "MGRS", "vertical_datum": "WGS84", "mgrs_grid": "54SUE"}); null when the map has none.

projector_type.description: The projection the Lanelet2 map was read with when the config overrode it (`map.projector_type`), else null: then `projector_info` decides.

mgrs_offset.description: [ox, oy]: the offset from CARLA's world frame to the Lanelet2 map frame, metres: x_map = x + ox, y_map = -y + oy (docs/trajectory_log.md). Null when no Lanelet2 map was loaded.

z_offset.description: The Lanelet2 map's elevation over CARLA's: z_map = z + z_offset, metres. Null when no Lanelet2 map was loaded.

TrafficLightRecord.title: TrafficLightRecord
TrafficLightRecord.description: A traffic light of the world, written once when recording starts.

opendrive_id.description: The light's signal id in the OpenDRIVE map; empty when CARLA could not tell.

location.description: The light actor's location in the world frame.

boxes.description: One box per light head. May be empty when CARLA could not tell.

stops.description: The waypoints of the light's stop lines. May be empty when CARLA could not tell.

WarmupRecord.title: WarmupRecord
WarmupRecord.description: Where the warm-up ended, written once, before the first tick (version 2). The ticks of the warm-up -- the run's settling, init actions and its wait for the ego to be ready -- are not in the file: the file starts where the scenario clock does, and the CARLA recording starts `ticks` frames earlier.

ticks.description: How many world ticks the warm-up took, from the CARLA recorder's start to the scenario clock's: the first `ticks` frames of the recording.

start_frame.description: The CARLA frame the recorder started at, or null when the run made no CARLA recording (then `ticks` is 0).

end_frame.description: The CARLA frame the scenario clock started at: the frame of the first tick record, at t = 0.

ActorRecord.title: ActorRecord
ActorRecord.description: A vehicle or walker, written right before the first tick it appears in: the ones there when recording starts, and every one spawned later. `actor_gone` says when it went.

type_id.description: The CARLA blueprint id; starts with "vehicle." or "walker.".

role.description: The actor's `role_name` attribute as set, case kept; empty when unset. "ego" or "hero" (any case) marks an ego, whose control inputs ticks carry.

extent.description: The bounding box's half size (x forward, y right, z up), metres.

center.description: The bounding box centre's offset from the actor origin, in the actor's own frame, metres.

ActorGoneRecord.title: ActorGoneRecord
ActorGoneRecord.description: A vehicle or walker that is no longer in the world (destroyed, or despawned by the traffic), written right before the first tick it is missing from (version 2). It is in no tick from then on.

frame.description: The CARLA frame of the tick it belongs to: the `frame` of a tick record (or of a tick left out for having no vehicle or walker in it).

t.description: That tick's simulated time, seconds since the scenario clock started.

TickRecord.title: TickRecord
TickRecord.description: The world right after one `world.tick()` (20 Hz). A tick without any vehicle or walker is not written, so `frame` and `t` can skip.

frame.description: The CARLA frame number of the snapshot, a uint64 in LibCarla.

t.description: Simulated seconds since the scenario clock started (the time pass/fail conditions see); not wall time.

actors.description: Every recorded vehicle and walker in the snapshot.

control.description: The last control applied to each ego, keyed by its actor id as a decimal string. Empty when there is no ego.

lights.description: The traffic lights whose state changed since the last written tick, keyed by actor id as a decimal string; every light in the first tick. Absent when none changed, so a reader carries each light's state forward.

MarkersRecord.title: MarkersRecord
MarkersRecord.description: The ego's debug markers (`EgoVehicle.debug_markers()`: a driver policy's planned trajectory, say), written after a tick when they changed (version 2): they hold from that tick until the next `markers` record. No polylines: the ego shows none from then on. A viewer of the run draws them beside the path the ego drove.

frame.description: The CARLA frame of the tick it belongs to: the `frame` of a tick record (or of a tick left out for having no vehicle or walker in it).

t.description: That tick's simulated time, seconds since the scenario clock started.

actor.description: The ego actor they belong to, or null when there was no ego actor on that tick.

polylines.description: The lines to draw, in order.

ConditionRecord.title: ConditionRecord
ConditionRecord.description: A pass or fail condition's state on a tick, written when it changes (version 2): on the first tick it is checked, then whenever it goes from satisfied to not or back. The run checks its conditions in order and stops at the first that decides it, so the last tick may leave later conditions out.

frame.description: The CARLA frame of the tick it belongs to: the `frame` of a tick record (or of a tick left out for having no vehicle or walker in it).

t.description: That tick's simulated time, seconds since the scenario clock started.

role.description: Which list the condition is in: a pass condition ends the run passed, a fail condition failed.

index.description: The condition's place in its list, from 0 (`pass[0]`, `fail[2]` in _result.json's labels).

label.description: The condition's label, as the scenario named it.

satisfied.description: Whether its check() reported it satisfied on that tick.

ActionRecord.title: ActionRecord
ActionRecord.description: A scenario action's lifecycle state on a tick, written when it changes (version 2): on the first tick of the loop, then whenever the action moves on -- `standbyState`, `startTransition` (the tick its trigger fired), `runningState`, `endTransition` (the tick it finished), `completeState`, or back to `standbyState` for a repeating action. The states are OpenSCENARIO's StoryboardElementState (`ActionState`). Init actions, run before the clock starts, are not written.

frame.description: The CARLA frame of the tick it belongs to: the `frame` of a tick record (or of a tick left out for having no vehicle or walker in it).

t.description: That tick's simulated time, seconds since the scenario clock started.

phase.description: Which list the action is in: `pre_tick` actions act before `world.tick()`, `post_tick` after it.

index.description: The action's place in its list, from 0: with `phase`, what identifies it.

label.description: The action's label, as the scenario named it.

AdversityRecord.title: AdversityRecord
AdversityRecord.description: An adversity NADE sampled on a tick (`AdversarialTrafficAction`, #397): who carries it out, what it is, the probabilities it was sampled with and the run's importance-sampling weight once it was. Written on the tick it was sampled; a run without NADE has none. Added in version 2, which a reader of version 2 that does not know it skips.

frame.description: The CARLA frame of the tick it belongs to, as an action record's.

t.description: That tick's simulated time, seconds since the scenario clock started.

label.description: The label of the action that sampled it.

agent.description: The role name of who carries it out.

location.description: Where it may fire, an `AdversityLocation` value.

probability.description: Its naturalistic probability p a tick, cut for an unavoidable one.

is_probability.description: The importance-sampling probability q it was sampled with.

weight.description: The run's importance-sampling weight once it was sampled, its victims' response included.

avoidable.description: Whether its victims could brake out of it.

victims.description: The NPCs that respond to it, by role name.

response.description: Their response: `avoid`, `accept`, or empty when none is driven (the ego is a victim).

WaypointArrivalRecord.title: WaypointArrivalRecord
WaypointArrivalRecord.description: A routed entity reached a waypoint that carries an arrival time or a departure condition (`RoutingAction`, any mode): when it was due and when it arrived, so a run can be scored on its timing. Written on the tick the arrival is known: on arrival for a time, and once the condition has held for a condition. Added in version 2, which a reader of version 2 that does not know it skips.

frame.description: The CARLA frame of the tick it belongs to: the `frame` of a tick record (or of a tick left out for having no vehicle or walker in it).

t.description: That tick's simulated time, seconds since the scenario clock started.

vertex.description: The waypoint's index among the route's vertices, from 0.

kind.description: What timed the waypoint: `time`, its arrival time, or `condition`, its departure condition (the target is the moment it first held).

mode.description: The routing mode: `driver` (the entity's own driver, paced by speed), `follow` or `position`.

target_t.description: Scenario time (s) the entity was due at the waypoint.

CollisionRecord.title: CollisionRecord
CollisionRecord.description: A vehicle other than the ego collided with a vehicle or a walker (`npc_collisions.NpcCollisionMonitor`): logged, not judged -- the ego's own collision condition is what fails a run. A contact is written when it begins (`phase: start`) and when it ends (`phase: end`, no event from the pair for a second), with how long it lasted. Added in version 2, which a reader of version 2 that does not know it skips.

frame.description: The CARLA frame the collision happened on.

t.description: That tick's simulated time, seconds since the scenario clock started.

actors.description: The `role_name` of each side (its type id when it has none): the vehicle that heard it first.

ids.description: The two actors' ids, in the order of `actors`.

impulse.description: The magnitude of the collision's normal impulse (N*s); at a contact's end, the strongest during it.

ego.description: Whether one side is the ego.

phase.description: `start` when the contact began, `end` when it ended.

duration.description: How long (s) the contact lasted, at its end; null at its start.

WalkerFallenRecord.title: WalkerFallenRecord
WalkerFallenRecord.description: A walker seen fallen over -- tipped beyond 50 degrees, or dropped more than half its height between two looks while barely moving sideways -- once per walker. It is left where it is. Added in version 2, which a reader of version 2 that does not know it skips.

frame.description: The CARLA frame of the tick it belongs to: the `frame` of a tick record (or of a tick left out for having no vehicle or walker in it).

t.description: That tick's simulated time, seconds since the scenario clock started.

role.description: Its `role_name` (its type id when it has none).

drop.description: How far (m) it dropped since the look before (0 when it tipped over without dropping).

tilt.description: How far (deg) it is tipped over: the larger of its pitch and roll.

SpawnRecord.title: SpawnRecord
SpawnRecord.description: A `SpawnAction` brought an entity into the scene (one spawned hidden, as a rule): put on its place, physics on, moving at its speed. Written on the tick it fired; the entity's `actor` record came earlier, when it was first seen hidden. A prop the action adds is not an entity and has no record. Added in version 2, which a reader of version 2 that does not know it skips.

frame.description: The CARLA frame of the tick it belongs to: the `frame` of a tick record (or of a tick left out for having no vehicle or walker in it).

t.description: That tick's simulated time, seconds since the scenario clock started.

id.description: Its actor's id; null if it is not known.

DespawnRecord.title: DespawnRecord
DespawnRecord.description: A `DespawnAction` (`reason: action`), or the run for a walker lying fallen 5 s (`reason: fallen`), took an entity out of the world: its traffic backend let go of it and its actor was destroyed. Written on the tick it fired. Added in version 2, which a reader of version 2 that does not know it skips.

frame.description: The CARLA frame of the tick it belongs to: the `frame` of a tick record (or of a tick left out for having no vehicle or walker in it).

t.description: That tick's simulated time, seconds since the scenario clock started.

id.description: Its actor's id; null if it had no actor.

reason.description: What removed it: `action` a DespawnAction, `fallen` a walker that lay fallen.

ResultRecord.title: ResultRecord
ResultRecord.description: The run's verdict, the last line of a run that ended with one (version 2): what _result.json says, but for each condition's details. A run that raised (or was interrupted) has none.

elapsed_seconds.description: The simulated time the verdict was reached at, seconds.

conditions.description: Every condition's final status, as _result.json lists them.

SafeUInt.description: A non-negative integer no larger than 2^53 - 1, so that every JSON reader holds it exactly, a double-only one (JavaScript) included. LibCarla's frame counter stays far below it; a value above it fails validation instead of losing precision.

UInt64.description: A non-negative integer of up to 64 bits.

ActorId.description: A CARLA actor id, a uint32 in LibCarla.

ActorIdKey.description: A CARLA actor id as an object key.

LightBox.title: LightBox
LightBox.description: [x, y, z, ex, ey, ez, yaw]: a light head's box centre in the world frame (m), its half size (m), and its yaw (deg).

StopWaypoint.title: StopWaypoint
StopWaypoint.description: [x, y, z, yaw]: a stop-line waypoint in the world frame (m) and its yaw (deg).

ActorState.title: ActorState
ActorState.description: [id, x, y, z, roll, pitch, yaw, vx, vy, vz]: the actor origin's location in the world frame (m), its rotation (deg), and its velocity in the world frame (m/s).

VehicleControl.title: VehicleControl
VehicleControl.description: [throttle, steer, brake, gear]: throttle and brake in [0, 1], steer in [-1, 1] (normalised, not an angle), gear an integer.

FileRef.title: FileRef
FileRef.description: A file the run read: where it was, and what it held.

path.description: Its absolute path on the machine that ran.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of its bytes, lowercase hex.

Polyline.title: Polyline
Polyline.description: A line through `points`, in CARLA's world frame (`DebugPolyline`).

points.description: Its vertices, in order, in the world frame (m).

point_size.description: The size of a dot drawn at each vertex, metres; none when 0.

ConditionStatus.title: ConditionStatus
ConditionStatus.description: A condition's state when the run ended (`ConditionStatus`, without its details).

label.description: Its label in _result.json: role, index and the condition's label, e.g. "pass[0](reached_goal)".

role.description: "pass" or "fail"; empty for a condition of neither list.

satisfied.description: Whether it was satisfied when the run ended.
